title: Choosing SQL or NoSQL for a workload

kcs.statement: Choose a relational database when the data is relational and you need joins, multi-row transactions or strict constraints, as with orders and payments; relational databases can also scale out with read replicas and sharding.

Choose a specific NoSQL store by comparing it on access pattern (lookup by a known key, whole-aggregate reads, partition-plus-range reads), schema flexibility, transaction scope, consistency options and built-in partitioning, not on the belief that only NoSQL scales.
A design may use several stores, each matched to one access pattern, for example SQL for orders, a key-value store for sessions and object storage for images.
